title: Pest insecticide, herbicide and fungicide management intervention monitoring and control processes

lessons.title: Supervising interventions in the workplace
lessons.html:
Stepping into the supervisor role

In this module you practise monitoring and controlling real insecticide, herbicide and fungicide interventions, first alongside your mentor and then leading small teams while your mentor observes. The aim is to make sure every job is done as planned, safely and effectively, and that problems are caught and corrected early.

What you will monitor on the job

  • That each team member treats only the planned areas and respects buffer zones.
  • That mixes are correct and match the calculation sheet.
  • That techniques, nozzles and pressures are correct.
  • That PPE is worn correctly throughout.
  • That weather remains suitable for outdoor work.
  • That occupants and animals stay out of treated areas.
  • That spills are prevented, or contained and reported.

Scenario: herbicide team on a farm

You supervise three workers spraying weeds along fence lines and around a silo hardstand. After an hour the wind rises and you notice fine spray moving towards a neighbour's vegetable garden. You stop the team, move them to an area where the wind blows away from sensitive plants, and resume the fence line later when the wind drops. You record the stop and the reason. One worker has removed his goggles because of sweat; you stop him and help him adjust them before continuing. This is the everyday reality of monitoring and control.

Communication

Agree stop signals before starting, stay within sight or radio contact of the team, and keep the client informed of progress and any incidents.

lessons.title: Follow-up, evaluation and evidence
lessons.html:
Evaluating results on real jobs

Return to sites at planned intervals to measure effectiveness, and practise analysing why a treatment worked or did not.

InterventionHow you evaluate it
Cockroach baiting in a kitchenSticky monitor counts, staff sightings, bait consumption
Rodent programme at a siloBait take per station, fresh droppings, trend graphs
Fence-line herbicidePercentage kill at the follow-up visit, regrowth
Fungicide on timber or plantsNew infection or decay compared with before

When results are poor

Work through the causes with your mentor: identification, product and rate, placement and coverage, weather after treatment, client actions such as cleaning or proofing, re-infestation and resistance. Agree corrective actions within label limits and record them.

Records you will keep

  • Application records with products, registration numbers, quantities and areas.
  • Stock reconciliation for each job.
  • Monitoring and evaluation data.
  • Incident reports and corrective actions.
  • Client service reports.

Portfolio evidence

Include records from jobs you supervised, mentor observation reports, an example trend analysis, and reflections on a problem you handled.

Key points

  • Monitor area, mix, technique, PPE, weather, people and spills throughout every job.
  • Stop and correct immediately when drift, unsafe behaviour or deviations occur, and record why.
  • Evaluate effectiveness with methods suited to each intervention.
  • Investigate poor results systematically and correct within label limits.
  • Keep complete records and mentor observations as evidence.

quiz.question: In the herbicide scenario, what did the supervisor do when spray drifted towards a vegetable garden?

options.text: Stopped the team and moved them to an area where drift was not a risk
Told the neighbour to cover the garden

quiz.question: A worker removes his goggles because of sweat. What should the supervisor do?

options.text: Stop him and help him adjust them before continuing

quiz.question: How would you evaluate a fence-line herbicide treatment?

options.text: Percentage kill and regrowth at follow-up

quiz.question: Why should a stop during a job be recorded?

options.text: To provide a record of what happened and why

quiz.question: Corrective actions after poor results must stay within...
Stop signals should be agreed before work starts.
Stock reconciliation is not needed if the job went well.
Which possible causes should be checked when results are poor? (select all that apply)

options.text: Client actions such as cleaning and proofing
